findings.reason: as written the gate can pass while the dead worker still holds the repair for ever, which is the exact defect the section was opened to repair.
findings.text: §9's done-when reads "The merge repair is not held, or is held with a reason naming the dead pid and the command that releases it", so a node can satisfy it by keeping the hold and only enriching the reason; nothing in the code names a release command, and the section's write paths (recovery_repair_dispatch.py and one test) cannot add one, so the second branch is both the behaviour §9 exists to remove and unimplementable within its scope

findings.reason: the plan's endpoint is that the cited 32/0 log agrees with its arm, and a count-only reading of "the whole gate" cannot reach it for any real suite arm.
findings.text: §11 makes only the failure count read across the whole gate, but `_receipt_mismatches` also compares `failure_ids` through `gate_log_failure_ids(..., last_run=True)`, and `ledger.suite_observation_missing_fields` refuses an arm with no `failure_ids` list, so the cited arm necessarily carries 32 ids that the clean last run does not report and the landing still refuses for its ids; the done-when's arm ("an arm recording 32") can omit ids and pass without touching that path, while the real imas-efit arm cannot

response_events.note: §9 drops the held-with-a-reason branch: a dead recorded pid releases the hold, and a live pid still holds it.
§11 now reads failure ids across the whole gate as well as the count, and its arm records 32 ids.
